headline: Morocco signs €270m AfDB financing for airport expansion
summary: The signed facility will modernise and expand Marrakech, Agadir, Tangier and Fez airports under the PEMIA programme.
why: Major DFI financing converts Morocco’s aviation-capacity strategy into funded upgrades across four strategic hubs.

headline: Kafue solar reaches $52.1m financial close in Zambia
summary: FMO and BII are providing long-term project finance for a 40 MWac plant backed by a 25-year ZESCO power-purchase agreement.
why: Financial close converts an eight-year development process into a construction-ready asset and tests delivery of Zambia’s wider GET FiT solar programme.

headline: Cameroon authorises €347.5m World Bank loan for Douala–Bangui corridor
summary: A presidential decree authorises signature of the IBRD credit agreement for Cameroon’s portion of the regional corridor programme.
why: The sovereign authorisation advances the largest national financing component of a corridor carrying over 80% of CAR’s external trade.

headline: IFC commits $50m to expand InfraCredit’s infrastructure-finance capacity
summary: A signed ten-year subordinated debt facility will strengthen InfraCredit’s capital base and mobilise long-term naira financing for infrastructure.
why: Loss-absorbing DFI capital can support a wider pipeline of locally financed projects through InfraCredit’s guarantee platform.

headline: EBID approves $100m for Kano–Maradi rail equipment
summary: The ECOWAS development bank approved a facility for rolling stock and operational equipment for Phase II of the standard-gauge railway.
why: Named financing for operating assets advances a major cross-border rail corridor beyond civil-works planning.

headline: Mercuria and Exergy sign $250m Zambia power investment deal
summary: Signed financing targets generation and transmission projects; funding remains subject to regulatory approvals.
why: Private capital from a global energy trader targets grid and generation assets with regional power-trade potential.

headline: Ethiopia–Djibouti launch $660m cross-border fuel corridor
summary: A 120-kilometre refined-products pipeline and major storage system will connect Damerjog with Dewele.
why: The sovereign-backed platform links port, pipeline, storage, rail and road infrastructure around Ethiopia’s fuel-supply chain.

headline: Dangote advances 700,000 BPD Kenya refinery with $450m-plus engineering mandate
summary: Engineers India will serve as PMC and EPCM consultant for the integrated greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex.
why: A signed delivery mandate moves one of Africa’s largest proposed downstream assets beyond concept and into structured engineering execution.

headline: DFC backs WIOCC’s pan-African digital-infrastructure platform
summary: U.S. development-finance capital targets wholesale connectivity, data centres and metro fibre across 30 African countries.
why: Institutional capital is moving into the enabling layer for cloud, telecom and enterprise expansion—not a routine operator upgrade.

headline: Nigeria moves its $300m distributed-energy fund from structuring to deployment
summary: Commercial launch creates a dedicated capital platform for mini-grids, standalone solar and other distributed-energy assets.
why: The fund has crossed from a planned vehicle into active deployment—an important test of scalable private-capital mobilisation for energy access.

headline: Baleine Phase 3 moves decisively into delivery
summary: New offshore awards activate engineering, fabrication, installation, drilling and specialist-services demand.
why: The project has moved beyond development intent into a broader offshore delivery ecosystem.

headline: US$2.33bn financing changes the Tanzania SGR execution picture
summary: Capital formation opens a new delivery window across rail construction and corridor logistics.
why: The commercial test is conversion of financing into procurement, mobilisation and visible construction.

headline: Bishoftu enters the build phase—and begins activating talent
summary: Groundbreaking, financing work and specialist hiring provide evidence of movement.
why: The opportunity now depends on project preparation converting into contracted delivery packages.

headline: Project BRIDGE enters investor prequalification
summary: A major digital-infrastructure programme creates an opening across fibre, financing and delivery partnerships.
why: Prequalification begins separating credible capital and delivery partners from general market interest.

headline: Lobito’s next test is financed construction
summary: The corridor’s value now depends on converting capital commitments into coordinated delivery.
why: Cross-border infrastructure creates commercial value only when financing and execution align across the system.
